key_insight: FurnitureVLA is the first systematic approach to real-scale bimanual furniture assembly with Vision-Language-Action models, extending robots beyond toy tasks into long-horizon, real-world assembly. The paper combines simulation, real-world teleoperation, and VLA learning to tackle complex multi-step manipulation.
problem_solved: Existing robot furniture assembly research mostly works at toy scale or with single-arm setups, which do not capture the difficulty of assembling real furniture. This paper addresses the challenge of learning long-horizon, bimanual assembly with scalable data collection and evaluation.
method: Formalizes real-scale bimanual furniture assembly as a learning problem for Vision-Language-Action models.
Develops a scalable simulation pipeline for expert demonstration generation and evaluation.
Builds a VR teleoperation system that lets one operator control both hands for high-quality real-world data collection.
impact: This work provides a practical foundation for training and evaluating robots on complex, multi-step assembly tasks that require coordinated two-arm manipulation. For AI/ML practitioners, it shows how to combine simulation, teleoperation, and VLAs to tackle long-horizon embodied tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing simulation data generation, VR teleoperation, and VLA training.

paper_title: FurnitureVLA: Learning Long-Horizon Bimanual Furniture Assembly with Vision-Language-Action Model
paper_authors: Chenyang Ma, Yue Yang, Radu Corcodel, Siddarth Jain, Andrew Wu
